findings.reason: The protected solution is clear, concise, and interview-ready. It uses one horizontal scalar, one in-place vertical array, and separate previous/current arrays for both diagonal directions. The row, column, directional-state, and longest names expose the four recurrences without a bulky per-cell table.

At each one-cell, the four states extend exactly the left, upper, upper-left, and upper-right predecessor; at a zero, horizontal and vertical state reset while the fresh diagonal arrays remain zero. Because diagonal reads come only from the previous row, no current update can corrupt a later dependency. Every legal line is therefore measured at its row-major endpoint.

Metadata consistently identifies Premium LeetCode problem 562 and its Python longestLine(mat) interface. The app-local solve(mat) accepts the binary rectangular matrix, returns a cell count, covers all four source directions, and defensively returns zero for an empty app input without altering the legal nonempty source domain.

The protected app source and immutable native source bound to verified submission 2065391126 are algorithmically identical: both allocate the same rolling arrays, reset on zero, extend the same four predecessors, update the same maximum, and rotate current diagonal state after each row.

The three all-one square workloads span 16 through 1024 cells and force long suffix rescans in the slower alternative. The exact protected source passed all 11 refreshed correctness cases and all three performance tiers, including legal 1 by 10000 and 10000 by 1 matrices. A correct control that started four fresh directional scans from every one passed every benchmark output but failed only scaling with relative growth exponent +0.41 and a 19.05x largest runtime ratio.

The Approach exactly matches the current rolling-state implementation and explains why fresh current-row diagonal arrays are necessary. Its complexity section now defines r and c, uses valid r times c notation, and correctly derives O(rc) time with O(c) auxiliary space.

The modular Reference was reviewed directly in the authenticated Premium statement and bound to its rendered live-content hash. It preserves all four permitted directions, both source matrices and outputs in order, the absence of prose example explanations, all five constraints, and both source visual relationships through independently authored accessible matrix tables.

coverage: Both authenticated Premium source examples now appear first and in source order. The truncated invented second sample was replaced by the exact three-row source matrix and its result 4.
The invented vertical-interruption sample was relabelled as a trial, and the formerly hidden anti-diagonal, competing-direction, and single-cell checks are now visible trials.

Contract boundaries cover 1 by 1, 1 by 10000, and 10000 by 1 matrices, the 10000-cell product maximum, both binary values, an all-zero matrix, and maximum-length one runs with and without a zero interruption.

Material semantics cover horizontal, vertical, main-diagonal, and anti-diagonal lines, zero resets, single rows and columns, competing directions, isolated ones, no-one results, fixed direction, and matrix-edge termination.

Independent scans that start only where each allowed direction enters the matrix verified all eleven correctness cases and all three benchmark outputs. The protected app and immutable native sources also agreed on 9,418 exhaustive small binary matrices and 1,000 randomized matrices.
All eleven correctness cases are visible samples or trials; the unchanged 4 by 4, 16 by 16, and 32 by 32 all-one workloads remain hidden and performance-only in benchmark.json.
